why: Confirmed by reading C:\claudecode\dark raiders\dark_raiders.html at v16.76 (HEAD 0b4cde2), with the queued p1679 in mind. Two faults make his report. (1) padFocusables (line 12002) lists button,.cell,.vcell,.crow,.invtab,.scard,.vpill,.sectorpick,input,select; the tactical belt keys that hotPlanHTML draws (line 32794) are plain <div data-plan=N> with no class, so the pad highlight can never land on a belt key on the Stash screen or the ascent check. (2) Pad A in padMenu is PAD.focus.click() (line 12115). On a backpack cell that is invCell's onclick, act(1) = leave one behind (unpack one); on a stash cell it is the v14.74 detail-0 branch, pack one. There is no pad grab state at all. The mouse does the move as a pointer drag: grabbable() (line 38724) sets GRAB={key,from,el} on mousedown and shows the ghost; the document mouseup (line 38757) finds the [data-drop] zone under the cursor and calls z.__grabDrop(held.key,held.from), which is the dropzone callback that holds every rule and message: the belt key dropzone in renderHub (planPut, rackPut, the v14.17 own-key clear, the v15.70 swap), the kitcol dropzone in renderKitCol (pack one from the stash, off the belt into the backpack, the full and only-have-N refusals) and the stashgrid dropzone (back in the stash, key cleared). The draft adds [data-plan] to padFocusables, and a pad grab that is the mouse press and the mouse drop: stashPadAct(el) with nothing held dispatches the very mousedown grabbable listens for on the highlighted cell (only on an element grabbable marked with cursor grab, so no synthetic press ever reaches a button, a dial or the HOLD TO CRAFT onmousedown), flags GRAB.pad, rings the cell (inset box-shadow, cleared in grabEnd) and puts the ghost on the highlight; with something held it calls the highlighted control's closest [data-drop].__grabDrop(key,from), the same function the mouse release calls, so every rule and word is the mouse one; let go on its own cell without a D-pad step between is the click a press and release in place sends, so A twice on a cell still does what one A did before (pack one, unpack one, clear a key). The ghost follows each highlight step (stashPadGhost, which also lights the target zone as mousemove does). B with a pad grab held runs grabEnd and returns before the back-out search, so it closes nothing on that press. A on an empty belt key with nothing held gets a pad sentence instead of the mouse hover hint (the mouse sentence is untouched; it is not in textedits.norm.json). Names mirror p1679 (bagPadAct/bagPadCell there; stashPadAct/stashPadGhost and GRAB.pad here, as G.drag.pad there); no anchor overlaps p1679. VER and the DEVNOW now line are left to the harness (this is the build after v16.79 in the queue); suggested now line: v16.80: A PICKS UP, A PLACES. His report from co-op: on the Stash screen a controller could only move things between the backpack and the stash, and the tactical belt was out of reach. Now A picks up the item under the highlight, the D-pad walks the highlight to a backpack cell, a stash cell or a belt key, and A there places it, exactly as a mouse drag does; B lets it go. Check 16.80 fails on v16.79.
